consensus_summary: Primary symbolism is God’s watchfulness/vigilance over His word, from the Jeremiah 1:11-12 Hebrew wordplay (shaqed/shoqed) reinforced by the almond as the earliest-blooming ‘wakeful’ tree. Common secondary strands are Aaron’s rod (divine election of priesthood, often with resurrection typology from the dead wood), the menorah’s almond-blossom cups (sanctuary light/divine presence), and Ecclesiastes 12:5 (white hair of old age).
book_summary: Almond is the watcher-tree (first to wake, from shaqad ‘to watch’: God watches over His word) and the priesthood’s sign (Aaron’s dead rod budded, blossomed and yielded almonds overnight as a resurrection sign choosing Levi); the sanctuary lampstand’s almond cups mean the watcher-tree bears the lamp.
consensus_core_identification: God’s watchfulness over His word (Jeremiah wordplay + early blooming), with secondary priesthood/resurrection and sanctuary-light associations
book_core_identification: Watcher-tree of divine watchfulness, priesthood’s resurrection sign via Aaron’s rod, and bearer of the sanctuary lamp
boundary_disagreement: none; book simply packages the same three main biblical occurrences without excluding or adding referents
rationale: Minimum cores are the same set of scriptural associations (Jeremiah watchfulness as chief, Aaron’s rod, and menorah almond cups). Book’s unified phrasing and the poetic link ‘watcher-tree bears the lamp’ are immaterial packaging differences, not a change of referent, boundary, or sense. Old-age reading is omitted but was already only an alternative, not core.
strongest_objection: The book’s tight compound identity and explicit claim that ‘the watcher-tree bears the lamp’ may over-integrate three contextually distinct passages beyond what the texts themselves require.
